name: BELEAGUERED CASTLE
description: Beleaguered Castle is a classic 'Open Packer' solitaire game where all 52 cards are visible from the start. The four Aces are stripped out to form the foundations (the 'Castle') in the center, and the remaining 48 cards are dealt into eight 'Wings' (side piles) of six cards each. The player must build the foundations up by suit from Ace to King, moving cards between the wings in descending sequence regardless of suit. It is a game of pure skill and deep calculation, often compared to FreeCell but without the safety net of empty transition cells.

content.text: Beleaguered Castle is a classic 'Open Packer' solitaire game where all 52 cards are visible from the start. The four Aces are stripped out to form the foundations (the 'Castle') in the center, and the remaining 48 cards are dealt into eight 'Wings' (side piles) of six cards each. The player must build the foundations up by suit from Ace to King, moving cards between the wings in descending sequence regardless of suit. It is a game of pure skill and deep calculation, often compared to FreeCell but without the safety net of empty transition cells.

First recorded in 1883 in William B. Dick's American collection 'Dick's Games of Patience', and it has appeared regularly in patience compendia since then. It is an open packer castle game closely related to other layout-focused solitaires.

One player (solitaire). The player acts alone: they remove the four Aces to form the foundations, deal the remaining 48 cards into eight wings, then move exposed cards between the tableau and foundations until all cards are built up or no legal moves remain.

1. Remove the 4 Aces and place them in a vertical column in the center (The Foundations). 2. Deal the remaining 48 cards face up into 8 horizontal rows (Wings) on either side of the Aces (4 rows left, 4 rows right). Each row has 6 cards overlapping so only the end card is accessible.

items.text: Citadel: Aces are not removed at the start. Instead, they are shuffled into the deck and must be played to the foundations as they become available.
Streets and Alleys: Similar to Citadel, but foundations are not placed in the center; they are built above the tableau.
